title: Structured output gating: interleaved tool-call recovery and chunked-stream schema enforcement
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reproducible evaluation and lightweight harness that verifies JSON-mode enforcement when model responses include interleaved tool/function calls and chunked streaming. This ticket focuses on: (1) deterministic detection of schema violations that occur across chunk boundaries, (2) simulated tool-call embedding that injects structured tool responses mid-stream, and (3) recovery strategies and telemetry to surface latent schema drift in production. The goal is a small, automated testbed that can be run in CI and as an offline regression benchmark for model onboarding and runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria: A harness exists that can replay model streams containing interleaved tool call tokens and verify final assembled payload against a provided JSON schema
Chunk boundary injection tests detect at least three classes of cross-chunk schema violations (truncated arrays, split strings, misplaced delimiters) and report deterministic failure reasons
Constrained-decoding hooks are exercised in the harness to validate that decoder backoff and sentinel insertion maintain schema validity for typical failure modes
Tests run in CI within a reasonable time budget (< 10m) and output machine-readable failure summaries linked to relevant test vectors
Telemetry events and error codes are defined so Console can show per-route schema regression counts and first-failure snippets
test_plan: 1) Generate a corpus of 300 synthetic prompts that combine structured response templates with simulated tool outputs (function call start/return tokens) and chunking patterns based on real token distribution traces. 2) Implement an assembler that reconstructs final JSON from partial chunks and verifies against JSON Schema and a relaxed tortoise parser for fuzzy acceptance. 3) Build constrained-decoding scenarios that intentionally trigger backoff and sentinel workflows and assert final contract satisfaction or graceful fallback. 4) Add CI job that runs a representative subset daily and full suite on release lanes.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Ticket created; scope agreed in sync with Runtime and Console leads
2025-02-14 - Prototype assembler implemented; initial round-trip tests for simple object payloads passing locally
2025-02-16 - Found two failure modes when simulating tool returns across chunk boundaries: missing closing array delimiter and truncated string escape sequences; added targeted fuzz vectors

2025-02-18 - Design review with PM and Runtime: decided to emit structured telemetry (schema_violation_type, first_bad_chunk_index, toolcall_marker_present) and wire to Console events. Luis to own PR for CI harness
2025-02-20 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8412 with assembler and 50 test vectors; initial CI flaky on one vector related to tokenizer split semantics (investigating)
steps: Implement streaming assembler that preserves metadata (chunk offsets, token indices, toolcall markers)
Create corpus generator based on production token-length distributions and common tool-call patterns
Define JSON Schema fixtures for typical server responses and edge-case schemas (nested arrays, large strings, optional tool-return fields)
Integrate constrained-decoding simulation to exercise decoder fallback/sentinel insertion
Add deterministic failure codes and map to Console telemetry schema
Add CI job and dashboard showing daily regression counts and top failing vectors
notes: Trade-offs: a strict assembler+schema check will surface more regressions but increase CI noise; we will provide a three-level severity mapping so teams can opt into strict blocking rules. We will iterate on tokenizer-aware chunking heuristics if too many false positives appear due to token-splitting inside escape sequences. This harness is intentionally scoped as a validation layer, not an attempt to fix model generation behavior; runtime mitigations (fallback model variants, cached prefixes) will be owned by serving infra follow-ups.
